title: gingiCHARM: a curated reference database and software package for whole-genome characterisation and multi-scheme typing of Porphyromonas gingivalis
access_conditions: Access is restricted during peer review. The repository will be made openly available on publication of the accompanying paper. Reviewers and editors should use the secret link supplied with the manuscript.
description:
gingiCHARM — P. gingivalis CHaracterisation, Allele typing and Reference Module

Falling sequencing costs have made whole-genome sequencing of oral anaerobes routine, but Porphyromonas gingivalis is absent from the typing platforms and virulence databases built around model organisms such as Escherichia coli, the streptococci and the staphylococci. Characterising a new P. gingivalis genome currently means assembling reference alleles by hand from four separate typing literatures published between 1998 and 2023, and writing a bespoke script for each scheme, repeated once per genome.

gingiCHARM provides a single curated reference database of 3,388 records together with six analysis modules:

  • pgvfdb — screening against 154 curated virulence-factor families (192 alleles)
  • fimtyping — fimA fimbrial types I–V
  • mfatyping — the complete mfa1–mfa5 minor-fimbriae operon profile
  • ragtyping — rag pathogenicity-island alleles rag-1 to rag-4
  • kantigen — capsular K-antigen serotypes
  • pgfunc — a ten-class functional category for every predicted gene

The reference set was built from five complete P. gingivalis genomes (ATCC 33277, W83, TDC60, A7436, AJW4), re-annotated with Bakta and clustered with MMseqs2 at 80% identity over 80% coverage into 2,616 non-redundant gene families, 1,476 of which are present in all five strains. Because Gene Ontology and KEGG annotate fewer than half of the P. gingivalis genome, the ten functional categories were curated specifically so that whole-genome enrichment analyses can be run across the full gene complement.

Validation against twelve reference-typed genomes returned the expected call from every typing scheme, and an independent in-silico PCR using published fimA typing primers agreed with the sequence-based call for every genome.

The package runs from a command line, as a Python API, or through a bundled Flask browser interface, and types a complete assembly in under a minute. Python 3.8 or later; NCBI BLAST+ is the only external dependency.
